title: Multipolar Light-Matter Hamiltonians in Symmetry-Breaking Photonic Vacuums
authors: Liu Yang, Jiadu Lin, Qing-Dong Jiang
abstract: We show that the conventional multipolar Hamiltonian is qualitatively modified when the photonic vacuum breaks inversion or time-reversal symmetry. By explicitly applying the Power-Zienau-Woolley transformation, we derive the resulting multipolar Hamiltonians for two idealized chiral photonic environments: a spatial-chiral vacuum, which breaks inversion symmetry, and a temporal-chiral vacuum, which breaks time-reversal symmetry. In the spatial-chiral case, the transformation generates an inversion-breaking self-energy, whereas in the temporal-chiral case it produces an additional Zeeman-like energy. Using a trapped hydrogen-like atom and a charged harmonic oscillator in cavities as minimal examples, we show that these symmetry-dependent terms lead to characteristic spectral shifts. Our work provides a general framework for describing light-matter interactions in chiral quantum electrodynamics and identifying the associated symmetry-dependent effects on cavity-embedded atoms, molecules, and quantum materials.
summary: This paper develops a generalized framework for light-matter interaction Hamiltonians when the photonic vacuum lacks inversion or time-reversal symmetry. By applying the Power-Zienau-Woolley transformation, the authors derive specific symmetry-breaking terms for chiral vacuums. These terms predict measurable spectral shifts in embedded atoms and molecules, advancing the theory of chiral cavity QED.
main_problem: The conventional multipolar Hamiltonian is insufficient for describing light-matter interactions when the surrounding photonic vacuum breaks inversion or time-reversal symmetry.
main_result: The symmetry breaking leads to new terms in the Hamiltonian, specifically an inversion-breaking self-energy in spatial-chiral vacuums and a Zeeman-like term in temporal-chiral vacuums.
method: The authors use the Power-Zienau-Woolley transformation to derive the modified multipolar Hamiltonians for idealized chiral photonic environments.
model_or_system: The analysis uses model systems such as trapped hydrogen-like atoms and charged harmonic oscillators coupled to spatially or temporally chiral cavities.
key_observables: Characteristic spectral shifts in embedded matter, including a second-order energy shift $\Delta E^{(2)}_{nS}$ and angular-momentum-dependent frequency shifts.
important_parameters: The coupling strength ($g/\omega_c$) and the nature of the vacuum symmetry ($\mathcal{I}$ or $\mathcal{T}$ breaking).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations, such as the long-wavelength limit and the dipole approximation for the Zeeman correction.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the mirror configurations for spatial-chiral and temporal-chiral vacuums, while Figure 3 compares normal-mode frequencies showing the effect of the Zeeman correction as coupling strength increases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for modification due to vacuum symmetry breaking, derives the general PZW Hamiltonians for the two chiral cases, and then applies these to model systems (hydrogen atom, harmonic oscillator) to calculate observable spectral shifts.
why_interesting: This work provides a general, rigorous framework for understanding how fundamental symmetries of the electromagnetic vacuum directly modify the fundamental light-matter coupling Hamiltonian in cavity QED settings.
